title: News Article
description:
Saw the name in a portal news headline.

"Real estate broker Im arrested on suspicion of defrauding multiple investors"

There was a photo. Definitely Im Sangchul.

Separate from what {name} did — another case had surfaced elsewhere. The father's situation wasn't the only one.

Closed the article and looked out the window. Learned a lot from that man. That man destroyed his father. Both things are true at once.

choices.text: Just moved past it. That relationship is over.
choices.result_text:
Closed the article. The connection with Im Sangchul ended at that café.

Who {name} is now — got here without his help, and without his weight.

choices.text: Called his father. He should know about this.
choices.result_text:
"Yeah." Father said briefly. "Good."

Nothing more. A short silence. Something heavy lifted slightly.

choices.text: Feeling sorry for him is strange
choices.result_text:
Without that man, the {name} now might not exist. But that man destroyed his father.

Both are true simultaneously. That's uncomfortable.

title: Three Years Later
description:
A KakaoTalk from Han Jiyeon.

"Long time no contact. How have you been since then?"

Then. The Im Sangchul introduction. Scalping. That intersection. Two years have passed.

Someone who briefly orbited close from a different life trajectory, then drifted as each got on with living.

choices.text: "I'm doing okay. Nice to hear from you." — straightforward
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon replied. "Glad to hear it. I've been shifting directions a bit myself. Let's meet sometime."

That was it. This relationship settled into something that exchanges occasional check-ins from the edges of each other's lives.

choices.text: "You helped me a lot back then. I think I've found my own way now." — honest
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon said "Oh really?" Then: "What way is that?"

Answering that question made the last two years fall into order. Strangely — in the process, Jiyeon said something similar. "I'm figuring that out too."

title: An Empty Chair
description:
Father's death anniversary.

No memorial table. In a Seoul goshiwon room — one photo of his father.

Still far from 3 billion won. What would he say if he knew?

"You worked so hard for this?" he might say. Or maybe "How did things turn out like this?"

{name} looked at the photo for a moment.

choices.text: "I'll get there, Father." — said it inwardly
choices.result_text:
The words came out.

No one heard. Father isn't here. Did it anyway. That's what's possible right now.

choices.text: Wanted to explain the current situation to him
choices.result_text:
I'm at this point, Father. Still far. But not giving up.

{name} said all of it silently. Every word felt important.

choices.text: Turned on the monitor. Living people have things to do.
choices.result_text:
The monitor came on. The charts came up.

The photo was still there. {name} was still there. Living people have things to do.

title: The Cost of Knowing
description:
Two months since the last conversation with Im Sangchul.

Today, a real estate consultant {name} met through Sangchul's network sent a message.
An independent deal, no direct connection to Sangchul. Good return conditions.

{name} paused when first seeing the name.
Knew exactly where that contact chain started.

Use it knowing — or cut this whole network loose?

choices.text: Use it. This is my network now. His crimes don't transfer to me.
choices.result_text:
Closed the deal. Money came in.

Sangchul's name hovered faintly next to the consultant's — but that's only something {name} knows.

choices.text: Not doing this deal. If it came from there, it all gets cut.
choices.result_text:
Declined. Didn't say why.

Hanging up, {name} thought of the first day arriving in Seoul.
That {name} wouldn't have known what this deal was. Now knows. So cut it.

choices.text: Do the deal — but this is the last one. The line gets drawn here.
choices.result_text:
Said "last one" silently.

Whether that word was real — the only way to know was when the next similar call came.

title: Not Her Father's Company
description:
Met up after a long stretch.

Over coffee, Han Jiyeon said:
"I've been studying for a real estate agent license."

{name} paused.

Her father runs a property firm. Her studying for the license herself was unexpected.

"For your father's business?"

choices.text: "Is it for your father's company?" — asked directly
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon smiled for a moment.
"No. I want something that's mine. Something that isn't the real estate boss's daughter."

That landed harder than expected.
{name} understood the weight of 'mine.'

choices.text: "That exam isn't easy, is it?" — realistic
choices.result_text:
"It's hard." Jiyeon said. "That's why I'm doing it."

Nothing more needed after that.
Doing something hard knowing it's hard — that's what sincerity looks like.

choices.text: "I think you'll do great." — kept it light
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon smiled lightly. "Thank you."

It was clearly a good thing to say — but after the conversation ended, {name} felt like something was unfinished.
The feeling of saying the easy thing instead of the right thing.

title: Different Directions
description:
A short text from Han Jiyeon.
"I'm heading to Busan. I'm going to open my own office there."

{name} read it about three times.
It wasn't sudden. She'd said she was studying, said she was finding direction.
But 'I'm going' still landed differently.

What was the right thing to say?

choices.text: "Take care. Sincerely." — let her go
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon replied. "Thanks. I'll message when I come back to Seoul."

That was the last text. A sincere goodbye is sometimes the most complete kind.
{name} locked the screen. Something felt properly finished.

choices.text: "You should have done this ages ago." — honest
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon replied after a moment. "You're right. It's late."
Then another message: "Still — glad it's now."

{name} had a feeling that wasn't only something she was saying to herself.

choices.text: "You could stay here, you know." — wanted to hold her back
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon didn't answer.
A short time later: just "Thank you."

That message felt like a goodbye. Trying to hold someone back doesn't keep them — it just makes them leave faster.

title: Making the Call First
description:
Sunday morning.

No reason. Nothing to do.
{name} picked up the phone. Put it down. Picked it up again.

Thinking back — in almost three years, had almost never reached out first.
There was always a contact coming in. {name} was always the one receiving.

Today, decided to call first. No reason at all.

choices.text: Called his father. No reason.
choices.result_text:
Father picked up.
"Oh, Minjun?" His voice was warm with surprise.

Nothing special was said. Weather talk, "Have you eaten?" talk.
After hanging up, {name} realized:
That was the reason. You don't need one.

choices.text: Called Hyunsu. Haven't heard from him in a while.
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu picked up. "Hey? {name}? Been a while."

"Yeah. What are you up to?" — "Just studying." — "Same." — "...Want to eat?" — "When?" — "This week?"

That was that. One call made first became a plan a month out.

choices.text: Pressed the call button. Then hung up. Not yet.
choices.result_text:
Hung up before it could ring.

{name} wasn't sure why.
Turned the phone face-down on the desk and looked out the window.

Calling first turned out to be harder than expected.

title: A Call from Busan
description:
A call from Han Jiyeon.

"Deal closed. Small villa. Goejeong-dong, Busan."

Her voice was different. Not light. First time hearing it since she left.
A year had passed.

Through the phone, faint sound of the ocean.

choices.text: "That's great. Genuinely. You made it happen."
choices.result_text:
A brief silence on the other end. Then Jiyeon said: "It feels more real hearing you say it."

Being someone who could say that to someone who made it — not a bad year.

choices.text: "Can I say I've missed you? After this long?"
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon laughed on the other end. "I wanted to hear that."

Said what went unsaid for a year. After hanging up, {name} lay looking at the ceiling for a long time.

The sound of the ocean was still there.

choices.text: "I'm holding on here too. Each in our own direction."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon said "Yeah." Short.

Different directions. The weight of those words when they were first written — still the same.
Two different cities. Two different staircases.

title: Briefly in Seoul
description:
Jiyeon came to Seoul. Two-day continuing education for licensed brokers.

Not a Cheongdam café. A neighborhood place nearby.

Jiyeon spoke first. "Seoul feels strangely unfamiliar. It's only been a year."

After two sips of coffee, she added: "Having you here makes it feel like Seoul again."

choices.text: "Come often then. I'll be waiting."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon smiled. The face she hadn't seen in a while.

"When can I come?" "Anytime."

They walked after leaving the café. No words — but not awkward. It felt like a lot had already been said.

choices.text: "Don't let this dismantle what you built in Busan. That's real, what you made there."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon was quiet for a while. Then: "Thank you."

"That's what I wanted to hear. Not to be held back."

The two of them living in different cities didn't feel wrong. Each standing in their own place — that's also a form of relationship.

choices.text: (Couldn't find words. That was the answer.)
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon stood up first. "I should get going."

Listening to the café door close, {name} looked at his coffee cup.

Unspoken words last longer than the ones you say.

title: Back to Seoul
description:
A text from Jiyeon.

"I've decided to open a Seoul branch. Gangnam. Next month."

Then one more line.
"I wanted to tell you first."

{name} looked at the text for a long time.
She's coming back because she grew wide enough in Busan — not because she narrowed.

choices.text: "See you in Gangnam. I'm on my way there too."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon replied: "Then I'll see you in Gangnam. For sure."

That became a promise. Neither of them was there yet. But both were heading there.

Seoul looked different somehow.

choices.text: "That decision has to be yours. Not because of me."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon replied after a moment: "I know. It's my decision. But you're one of the reasons."

That was honest. There's a reason honest is good.

title: Word from Busan
description:
Word came through a mutual contact.

Han Jiyeon. Doing well in Busan. Has staff now. Made a name in the area.

And — she's seeing someone from Busan.

{name} paused.
Whether that was good news, or something else — the feeling didn't have an exact name.

choices.text: "That's great." — said it sincerely
choices.result_text:
Meant it.

Jiyeon is building her own thing in Busan. That was the point. She reached it.

Different directions — at first it felt like goodbye. Now it feels like it was the right phrase.

choices.text: (Nodded. Nothing to say.)
choices.result_text:
Nodded.

Nothing to say. More precisely — there was something that couldn't be said right now, and that was all.

{name} started walking. Seoul was the same as always.

description_if_known.jiyeon_respectfully_distanced:
Word came through a mutual contact.

Han Jiyeon. Doing well in Busan. Has staff now. Made a name in the area.

And — she's seeing someone from Busan.

{name} paused. Back in Seoul, they'd been honest — said there was someone. After that, Jiyeon had seemed lighter. Smiled more easily. Talked more freely about herself.

Because the goodbye was clean — this news could land as something good.
description_if_known.jiyeon_hidden_feelings:
Word came through a mutual contact.

Han Jiyeon. Doing well in Busan. Has staff now. Made a name in the area.

And — she's seeing someone from Busan.

{name} paused. Back in Seoul, they'd chosen silence. Said nothing. What shape that silence had taken by now — the feeling didn't have an exact name.

title: Briefly in Seoul (Two Hearts)
description:
Jiyeon came to Seoul. Two-day continuing education for licensed brokers.

The same café. Jiyeon spoke first. "Seoul feels strangely unfamiliar. It's only been a year."

After two sips of coffee, she added: "Having you here makes it feel like Seoul again."

{name} paused.
Knew the weight of those words. And also — knew there was already someone else.

choices.text: Said it honestly. "I'm seeing someone right now."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon was quiet for a moment. Then smiled. "I know. I just mean — you're a good person."

They finished their coffee. It wasn't awkward.

Learned that day — honest words don't break things.

choices.text: (Said nothing. Let her misread it.)
choices.result_text:
Said nothing.

Jiyeon smiled and stood up. "See you again."

{name} sat there. The gap between 'not being honest' and 'lying' — narrower than expected.
